models.name: discussion_board_guests
models.description: Temporary guest accounts for anonymous platform access. Guests browse sections and view public articles without registration. Identified by device fingerprint for session continuity across page loads. No authentication required, but actions are attributed to the device for basic personalization and rate limiting.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device identifier (browser fingerprint, user-agent, or similar) that identifies this guest across requests.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest identity was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest record was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access without authentication credentials.

This table tracks login sessions for guest actors identified by device fingerprint. Each session stores connection metadata (IP address, current URL, referrer) and temporal information for session lifecycle management. Sessions are created when a guest authenticates and terminated on logout or expiration.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to {@link discussion_board_guests} - one-to-many relationship where a guest can have multiple sessions over time (but only one active at a time per session lifecycle requirements)
- Session tokens are used for JWT-based authentication
- Connection metadata supports security auditing and abuse detection

**Behavioral Notes**:
- Sessions expire after configured timeout (30 minutes inactivity)
- New login terminates existing session (one active session per guest)
- Append-only table - sessions are never updated, only created and logically expired
- Used for tracking guest access patterns and security monitoring

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged guest's {@link discussion_board_guests.id}. References the guest account this session belongs to.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client device when the session was created. Used for security auditing and abuse detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current URL (href) of the page when the session was created. Tracks the entry point for the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the session creation. Used for tracking traffic sources and security analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for session expiration calculation and audit trail.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. NOT NULL for security - ensures all sessions have a defined expiration time.

models.name: discussion_board_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email and password authentication credentials.

Members are authenticated users who can create articles, write comments, manage their profile, submit administrator requests, and participate in community discussions. Each member has a unique email address for login, a hashed password for security, and optional profile information including display name and bio.

Members can be banned by administrators, which prevents login while preserving their existing content. When a member deletes their account, all their articles and comments are also deleted. Members can request to become administrators through the admin request system.

Key relationships:
- Owns {@link discussion_board_articles} - articles created by the member
- Owns {@link discussion_board_comments} - comments written by the member
- Owns {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} - admin privilege requests submitted by the member
- Subject of {@link discussion_board_ban_records} - ban actions applied to the member
- Has {@link discussion_board_member_sessions} - active authentication sessions
- Has {@link discussion_board_member_password_resets} - password reset tokens

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for member authentication and login.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for member authentication. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown on articles, comments, and profile pages.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biographical text displayed on the member's profile page.

plainFields.name: banned
plainFields.description: Whether the member account is currently banned and cannot log in.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted. Null means account is active.

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description: JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh token support. Tracks active login sessions for member accounts, recording connection metadata and temporal boundaries for security auditing and session management.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the authenticated member account. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client device during session creation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the page that initiated the authentication flow.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header from the authentication request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session token expires.

models.name: discussion_board_member_password_resets
models.description: Stores time-limited, single-use tokens for member account password recovery. Each record represents a password reset request with an expiring token that can be used exactly once to verify identity and allow password change without requiring current credentials.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_members_id
foreignFields.description: References the member account requesting the password reset. Links to {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token for password reset verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was initiated.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token expires.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was successfully used. Remains null if token is still valid and unused.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string from the original password reset request for security auditing.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from the original password reset request for security auditing.

models.name: discussion_board_administrators
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email and password authentication and elevated privileges.

This table stores administrator user accounts with authentication credentials and privilege levels. Administrators have two grades: regular administrator and super administrator. Super administrators have the authority to promote/demote other administrators and manage section organization.

Key relationships:
- Owns `discussion_board_ban_records` for user suspension actions
- Manages `discussion_board_sections` for content organization
- Reviews `discussion_board_admin_requests` for privilege escalations
- Owns `discussion_board_administrator_sessions` for active login sessions

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for administrator authentication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash for administrator authentication.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Display name shown in the interface.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Short biographical text for the administrator profile.

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: Administrator grade: 'regular' or 'super'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to this record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the account was logically deleted (soft delete).

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with access and refresh token support.

This table tracks active login sessions for administrators, storing connection metadata, JWT token hashes, and expiration information. Each administrator can have only one active session at a time, ensuring secure single-device access.

Key relationships:
- References {@link discussion_board_administrators} to associate the session with the authenticated administrator
- Uses unique constraint on administrator_id to enforce single active session policy

Security features:
- Stores token hashes instead of raw tokens for security
- Tracks access token (15-minute expiration) and refresh token (7-day expiration)
- Records connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) for audit trail
- expired_at field indicates session termination (logout, expiration, or forced invalidation)

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}. Enforces one active session per administrator.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the administrator logged in. Used for security auditing and session validation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL or endpoint where the administrator initiated the session. Used for tracking session origin.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the authentication page. Used for security analysis and audit trail.

plainFields.name: access_token_hash
plainFields.description: Hash of the access token (15-minute expiration). Stored as hash for security, not the raw token.

plainFields.name: refresh_token_hash
plainFields.description: Hash of the refresh token (7-day expiration). Stored as hash for security, enables token refresh without re-authentication.

plainFields.name: access_token_expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the access token. Typically 15 minutes from session creation.

plainFields.name: refresh_token_expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the refresh token. Typically 7 days from session creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Records the login time for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was terminated. Set on logout, token expiration, or forced invalidation. Null indicates active session.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for administrator account recovery. Each record represents a one-time, time-limited token sent to an administrator's email for secure password recovery. The token is single-use and expires after a short period for security. When a token is used, it is marked as consumed and cannot be reused.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrators_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator account requesting the password reset. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure random token sent to administrator email for identity verification during password reset flow.

plainFields.name: token_type
plainFields.description: Type of token operation. Distinguishes between 'password-reset' and other potential token types for extensibility.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token expires for security. Tokens are time-limited to prevent replay attacks.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this token was redeemed for password reset. Null if not yet used, set to current time when token is consumed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token was generated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_sections
models.description:
Organizational containers for grouping articles by topic within the discussion board.

Sections serve as the primary categorization mechanism for articles, allowing users to browse content by subject matter (e.g., Politics, Economy, Current Affairs). Each section has a unique name and optional description that explains its purpose and scope.

**Management**: Sections are created, edited, and deleted exclusively by administrators. Regular users and guests can only view sections and browse articles within them.

**Relationships**:
- One-to-many with {@link discussion_board_articles}: Each section can contain multiple articles, and each article belongs to exactly one section.
- Managed by {@link discussion_board_administrators}: Only administrators have permission to modify sections.

**Business Rules**:
- Section names must be unique across the entire board to prevent confusion.
- Sections cannot be deleted if they contain articles (referential integrity).
- Section modifications are tracked in {@link discussion_board_section_snapshots} for audit purposes.
- Soft delete is supported via `deleted_at` field to preserve historical data.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique name of the section used for identification and display. Must be distinct from all other sections.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description explaining the section's purpose, scope, and guidelines for content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was soft deleted. Null indicates the section is active.

models.name: discussion_board_section_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of section modifications for audit trail and revision history.

This table captures the complete state of a section at the moment of modification, preserving historical data for compliance and audit requirements. Each record represents a specific version of a section, enabling version control, change tracking, and historical analysis of section configurations.

Key characteristics:
- Immutable records: Once created, snapshots are append-only to maintain an accurate audit trail
- Complete state capture: All section properties are denormalized to preserve exact historical state
- Reference model: {@link discussion_board_sections}

Temporal field semantics:
- section_created_at: When the original section was created (from parent)
- section_updated_at: When the section was last modified before this snapshot (from parent)
- created_at: When this snapshot was taken

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_sections_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the section being snapshot. {@link discussion_board_sections.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Name of the section at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of the section at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: section_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the original section was created (captured from parent).

plainFields.name: section_updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last modified before this snapshot (captured from parent).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Main entity storing article content for the discussion board platform.

Articles are the primary content units that users create, organize by sections, and engage with through comments. Each article contains a title and full text content, belongs to exactly one section, and is authored by a registered member.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a {@link discussion_board_sections} for organizational categorization
- Owned by a {@link discussion_board_members} who created it
- Created through a {@link discussion_board_member_sessions} for audit trail
- Has many {@link discussion_board_comments} (handled in Comments component)
- Has many attachments (handled in Attachments component)
- Has many {@link discussion_board_tags} via junction table (handled in Tags component)

Articles support soft deletion to preserve historical data while removing from active listings. Administrators can delete any article regardless of authorship for content moderation purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged section's {@link discussion_board_sections.id}. Every article must be assigned to exactly one section for organizational categorization.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Author member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Tracks which registered user created and owns this article.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Creation session's {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id}. Records the authentication session used when creating the article for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title. Required field that identifies the article in listings and search results.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full text content of the article. Required field containing the main body text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was first created. Used for chronological sorting and display.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was last modified. Updated on every edit operation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was soft-deleted. Null indicates the article is active. Used for soft deletion to preserve historical data.

models.name: discussion_board_article_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of articles for audit trail and revision history.

This table captures the complete state of an article at specific moments in time, enabling:

- **Audit Trail**: Track all modifications made to articles over time
- **Revision History**: View previous versions of article content
- **Accountability**: Maintain record of what content existed when

Each snapshot is created when an article is modified (title, content, section assignment, or author changes). Snapshots are immutable historical records that preserve the exact state of the article at the time of capture.

**Key Relationships**:
- References {@link discussion_board_articles.id} as the parent article being snapshot
- References {@link discussion_board_members.id} as the article author at snapshot time
- References {@link discussion_board_sections.id} as the section assignment at snapshot time
- References {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id} as the session context at snapshot time

**Business Context**:
- Snapshots are append-only and never modified or deleted
- Multiple snapshots exist per article (one per modification event)
- Used for compliance, auditing, and potential content restoration

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id} that this snapshot captures.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Article author's {@link discussion_board_members.id} at the time of snapshot.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Article section's {@link discussion_board_sections.id} at the time of snapshot.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session's {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id} used when the article was modified, captured for audit trail.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Article content captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

models.name: discussion_board_article_views
models.description:
Individual view events for articles, tracking when and by whom articles were accessed.

This table records each view event to enable engagement analytics, popular content identification, and user reading history. Each record represents a single view occurrence, supporting both authenticated member views and anonymous guest access.

Key relationships:
- References {@link discussion_board_articles.id} to identify which article was viewed
- Optionally references {@link discussion_board_members.id} for authenticated views
- Optionally references {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id} to track the session context

Used for:
- Analytics dashboards showing article popularity
- User reading history and recommendations
- Engagement metrics and trending content identification

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Viewing member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}, null for guest views.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Viewing session's {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id}, null for guest views.

plainFields.name: viewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was viewed.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id

models.name: discussion_board_admin_requests
models.description:
Administrator privilege escalation requests submitted by members seeking elevated permissions.

This table tracks the lifecycle of admin promotion requests from submission through review and decision. Members submit requests with a reason explaining why they should become administrators. Super administrators review these requests and approve or reject them.

Each request maintains its status (pending, approved, or rejected) along with submission and review timestamps. The request references both the submitting member and the reviewing administrator (when applicable).

**Key Relationships:**
- Submitted by: {@link discussion_board_members} - The member requesting admin privileges
- Reviewed by: {@link discussion_board_administrators} - The super administrator who made the decision (nullable for pending requests)
- Decision details: {@link discussion_board_admin_request_decisions} - Detailed approval/rejection context stored separately

**Status Workflow:**
1. `pending` - Request submitted, awaiting review
2. `approved` - Request approved, member promoted to administrator
3. `rejected` - Request rejected, member remains regular user

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who submitted the admin privilege request. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator who reviewed and decided on this request. Nullable for pending requests. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The member's explanation for why they should become an administrator. Required field that justifies the privilege escalation request.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the admin request. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (member promoted), 'rejected' (request denied).

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member submitted this admin privilege request.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator reviewed and made a decision on this request. Null for pending requests.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was soft-deleted. Null indicates active record.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_request_decisions
models.description:
Super administrator approval or rejection decisions with context for admin requests.

This table captures the decision event when a super administrator reviews and processes a pending administrator privilege escalation request. Each decision is immutable and serves as an audit trail record.

**Key Relationships**:
- Belongs to exactly one {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} (1:1 relationship via unique constraint)
- Made by exactly one {@link discussion_board_administrators} (the super administrator reviewer)

**Business Rules**:
- Only super administrators can create decisions
- Each admin request can have at most one decision (pending requests have none)
- Once a decision is recorded, the request status changes and no further decisions are allowed
- Decisions are immutable audit records that cannot be modified or deleted

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_request_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator request's {@link discussion_board_admin_requests.id}. Each decision applies to exactly one request.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator who made the decision's {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}. Only super administrators can approve or reject requests.

plainFields.name: decision_type
plainFields.description: The decision outcome: 'approved' or 'rejected'. Determines whether the requesting user becomes a regular administrator.

plainFields.name: decision_context
plainFields.description: Optional additional notes or context provided by the super administrator when making the decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision was made. This is the official review timestamp recorded for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was last modified. For immutable audit records, this typically equals created_at.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision was soft deleted. Nullable for active decisions, set when record is logically removed.

models.name: discussion_board_ban_records
models.description:
Audit trail of user ban actions with reasons, timestamps, and administrator attribution.

This table tracks all user suspension actions on the discussion board platform. Each record captures when a user was banned, the reason for the ban, which administrator imposed it, and when (if ever) the ban was lifted.

The table uses a polymorphic ownership pattern to support banning both members and administrators. The actor_type field distinguishes between the two actor types, with separate subtype tables (discussion_board_ban_record_of_members and discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators) maintaining the actual foreign key relationships.

Key relationships:
- {@link discussion_board_administrators}: Administrator who imposed the ban
- {@link discussion_board_ban_record_of_members}: Member-specific ban details (1:1)
- {@link discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators}: Administrator-specific ban details (1:1)

This table serves as the authoritative record for moderation accountability and enforcement history.

foreignFields.name: banned_by
foreignFields.description: Administrator who imposed the ban. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor being banned. Either 'member' or 'administrator'. Used with subtype tables for polymorphic ownership.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Required reason explaining why the user was banned. Must contain detailed explanation of policy violation or harmful behavior.

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was imposed. Recorded automatically when ban action is executed.

plainFields.name: unbanned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was lifted. Null if the ban is still active.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was soft deleted. Used for audit trail preservation.

models.name: discussion_board_ban_record_of_members
models.description:
Subtype table for member ban records implementing polymorphic ownership pattern.

This table links ban records to specific member accounts with a 1:1 relationship. It is part of the polymorphic ownership design where ban records can apply to different actor types (members or administrators) through separate subtype tables.

**Key Characteristics**:
- Each ban record references exactly one member via unique foreign key
- Each member can have at most one active ban record
- Stores the session information of the administrator who performed the ban for audit trail
- No duplicate temporal fields - accessed via parent ban record

**Relationships**:
- {@link discussion_board_ban_records.id} - Parent ban record (1:1)
- {@link discussion_board_members.id} - Banned member account (1:1)
- {@link discussion_board_administrator_sessions.id} - Session of administrator who performed the ban (optional, for audit)

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_ban_record_id
foreignFields.description: Parent ban record's {@link discussion_board_ban_records.id}. Establishes 1:1 relationship with the main ban record entity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Banned member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Links the ban record to the specific member account being banned.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_session_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator session's {@link discussion_board_administrator_sessions.id} that performed the ban action. Used for audit trail to track which administrator session executed the ban.

models.name: discussion_board_ban_record_of_administrators
models.description:
Subtype table linking ban records to administrator accounts.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for ban records, specifically handling cases where an administrator account is banned. It maintains a 1:1 relationship with the main ban record entity, ensuring each ban record is associated with exactly one actor type.

The table stores the reference to the banned administrator's account, enabling proper tracking of which administrator was suspended, while the main ban record stores the reason, timestamp, and banning administrator.

**Key Relationships**:
- Links to {@link discussion_board_ban_records.id} with unique constraint (1:1)
- References {@link discussion_board_administrators.id} for the banned administrator

**Usage Pattern**:
- Created when an administrator is banned
- Maintains audit trail of administrator suspensions
- Works in conjunction with discussion_board_ban_record_of_members for complete ban tracking

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_ban_record_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the main ban record. {@link discussion_board_ban_records.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the banned administrator account. {@link discussion_board_administrators.id}

models.name: discussion_board_tags
models.description:
Master table storing unique tag names for article categorization and filtering.

This table maintains the canonical list of all tags used across the discussion board system. Each tag represents a free-text label that can be assigned to articles for organizational purposes. Tags are created dynamically when users assign them to articles, with no predefined vocabulary or approval process required.

Key characteristics:
- Tags are free-text with no length restrictions
- Tag names are case-sensitive and preserve exact user input
- Multiple articles can share the same tag
- Tags exist independently of articles and persist even when all associated articles are deleted
- Used for article filtering, search, and categorization across the platform

Related entities:
- {@link discussion_board_article_tags}: Junction table linking tags to articles (many-to-many relationship)
- {@link discussion_board_articles}: Articles that can have multiple tags assigned

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The tag name as entered by the user. Preserves exact text including capitalization and spacing. No predefined vocabulary or validation against allowed values.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was first created and added to the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was soft deleted. Null indicates the tag is active.

models.name: discussion_board_article_tags
models.description:
Junction table for the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags.

This table enables free-text tag assignment to articles for categorization, filtering, and search functionality. Each record represents a single tag assignment to an article.

Key characteristics:

- **M:N Relationship**: Links {@link discussion_board_articles} to {@link discussion_board_tags}
- **No Duplicates**: Composite unique constraint prevents assigning the same tag to an article multiple times
- **Tag Filtering**: Supports filtering articles by specific tags
- **Audit Trail**: Created_at timestamp tracks when tags were assigned

Usage patterns:

- When creating an article with tags, insert records into this table
- When editing article tags, delete old assignments and insert new ones
- When deleting an article, all associated records are cascade-deleted

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: References the article this tag is assigned to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_tag_id
foreignFields.description: References the tag assigned to this article. {@link discussion_board_tags.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was assigned to the article.
